documents.title: Condition and maintenance history
documents.text:
Condition and maintenance history, compiled by Eleanor Whitcomb.
Before the tenancy: the apartment was painted and the floors redone in late 2022. Karen Liu's 2022 listing photographs show intact fireplace tiles and window woodwork, and good floors with a few dark spots and one diagonal scratch in the living room. A family stayed briefly over the 2022 holidays before the Brenners moved in on January 9, 2023.
June 11, 2024: Laura Brenner emailed 22 photographs of screens, a loose dining-room hearth, loose or broken tiles, missing molding and a small missing parquet piece, describing them as existing on arrival. None of this was reported within the two days required by rider ¶14.
Complaints during the tenancy: uneven room temperatures, a clogged toilet, a roof leak, weak dryer performance, bin lids and the intercom. Work done: screens repaired, window weather stripping and five temperature sensors added, a new intercom installed and the leaks repaired.
June 2024: during a screen inspection Eleanor found a dog accident on the floor; Laura apologized and cleaned it up.
Repeated indoor grilling caused grease odors and set off smoke alarms. Eleanor asked the Brenners to stop.
August 2026: a slow leak under the kitchen sink damaged the cabinet base and subfloor. Feld Architecture managed the repair: new supply lines and shutoff valves, a replaced sink base and a patched subfloor. Work finished August 21; Feld signed it off on August 24 after a moisture check. No further work is needed.

documents.title: Move-out walk-through, September 24, 2026
documents.text:
Move-out walk-through, September 24, 2026. Present: Eleanor Whitcomb (owner), Michael Brenner (tenant), Karen Liu (broker) and Paul Novak. Eleanor took 60 photographs; Paul recorded a video.
Entrance and stairs: front step chipped; saddle past the vestibule gouged with a broken corner; common-foyer mahogany door with veneer sheared off one section; newel post chipped and gouged; stair carpet edges scraped and torn on several steps; top molding and rail edge damaged between the second and third floors.
Living room: parquet scraped, scratched and gouged; decorative border missing inlay pieces and stained; finish worn through in places.
Dining room: paint blotches, gouges and a large stain on the parquet; damaged parquet corners; antique hearth tiles missing and broken; mahogany mantel damaged; a large piece of the doorway casing damaged or missing.
Office: carpet heavily stained; floor scratched. Mahogany window sills throughout: stains, ring marks and gouges.
West master suite: large dark stains on the plank floor, including in front of the fireplace, with a urine odor; scrapes and gouges; soot staining on the wall, ceiling, mantel and shelving; a deep gouge in the molding.
East master bedroom: ceiling damaged where the period chandeliers were replaced with the tenants' fixtures. East bathroom ceiling stained and damaged.
Third floor: southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing pulled away, with protruding nails and torn wood; not safe to use. Northeast storage-ladder railing scraped. Northeast bedroom plank floor with a dark urine stain; bedroom door broken and the plaster behind it damaged. Bathroom tub porcelain chipped and vanity panel broken. Great-room plank floor heavily stained and gouged with a urine odor; plaster damage and staining down one wall; ceiling damaged around the light fixtures.
Karen Liu also noted odors in several rooms.

I want the triplex back on the market as soon as possible, ideally showing by late October for a December 1 move-in.

workPlan.title: Triplex restoration and floor and stair finishes
workPlan.summary: Authorize (1) Westside Plaster & Paint for plaster/soot cleanup, painting, woodwork and fireplace restoration, and bathroom repairs; (2) Hudson Floor Restoration for parquet and plank floor repair/refinishing including inlay replacement and urine-stain treatment/sealing; (3) Carroll Stair & Millwork for main stair repair/refinishing; and (4) Broadway Carpet & Runner for new stair runner and office carpet replacement after finish work is complete.
workPlan.desiredOutcome: Restore the triplex to a clean, safe, show-ready condition for the next occupant by correcting the documented move-out deficiencies in finishes, floors, stair millwork, stair runner, and office carpet, and addressing urine staining/odor sources in the flooring.
scope: Plaster repair and soot cleanup in the great room, northeast bedroom and west master suite, including patching damaged plaster and cleaning/sealing soot-stained surfaces.
Repair ceilings at light fixtures as needed, then prime and paint walls, ceilings and trim throughout the triplex.
Repair and refinish damaged mahogany woodwork and fireplaces, including window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels, damaged hearth tiles, foyer door veneer, and the northeast bedroom door.
Repair the third-floor tub porcelain chip, refit/repair the vanity panel, and complete bathroom caulking/touch-ups as needed.
Sand and refinish parquet and plank floors in the triplex, stain to match, and apply finish coats per the quote.
Replace damaged parquet and missing inlay border pieces with matched stock, including cutting out damaged pieces and setting replacements.
Treat urine-stained plank floors and seal prior to refinishing to reduce staining and address odor source areas.
Repair and refinish the main stair, including newel post, trim, top molding and rail edge, restoring damaged/chipped areas and finish.
Supply and install a new stair runner after stair work is complete.
Replace the office carpet after finish work is complete.
workPlan.rationale: The move-out walk-through and Feld Architecture’s restoration assessment report document damaged/stained floors with missing inlay, urine odor areas, damaged plaster/ceilings/paint, damaged mahogany woodwork and fireplaces (including hearth tiles and doors), chipped tub/vanity defects, and chipped/damaged stair millwork plus torn stair runner and heavily stained office carpet. This plan funds the quoted trade scopes that directly match those items, without duplicating the already-completed loft ladder railing repair and assessment. Recommended sequencing: Westside first (plaster/paint/woodwork/bath), then Hudson floors, then Carroll stair refinishing (with floor protection), and Broadway runner/office carpet last.

content.rationale: The move-out condition notes identify a dangerous, pulled-away loft-ladder railing that should be made safe before anyone uses that ladder. Separately, the owner’s written instruction is to have Feld Architecture walk the apartment first and deliver a condition schedule and scoped budget before committing to broader repairs. This proposal does both, within the owner’s restoration funds set aside.

selections.scope: Feld Architecture site visit (up to 3 hours) to inspect all rooms, photograph/measure conditions, and flag safety issues.
selections.reason: Owner directed that Feld walk the apartment first before we authorize broader restoration work. This is the “Site assessment” line in Feld Architecture’s “Restoration assessment” quote (Restoration assessment document).

selections.scope: Feld Architecture written scope by trade with a preliminary budget based on observed conditions.
selections.reason: Provides the trade-by-trade scope and preliminary budget the owner requested so we can decide what to authorize and in what sequence. This is the “Scope and budget note” line in Feld Architecture’s “Restoration assessment” quote (Restoration assessment document).

selections.scope: Carroll Stair & Millwork rebuild and secure the southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing and test it under load, making the ladder access safe to use.
selections.reason: The move-out walk-through notes the loft-ladder railing is pulled away with protruding nails and is unsafe; the owner explicitly directed keeping off that ladder until it is fixed. This line directly resolves the safety hazard (Loft railing repair quote document).

content.title: Triplex restoration and floor and stair finishes
content.summary: Authorize (1) Westside Plaster & Paint for plaster/soot cleanup, painting, woodwork and fireplace restoration, and bathroom repairs; (2) Hudson Floor Restoration for parquet and plank floor repair/refinishing including inlay replacement and urine-stain treatment/sealing; (3) Carroll Stair & Millwork for main stair repair/refinishing; and (4) Broadway Carpet & Runner for new stair runner and office carpet replacement after finish work is complete.
content.desiredOutcome: Restore the triplex to a clean, safe, show-ready condition for the next occupant by correcting the documented move-out deficiencies in finishes, floors, stair millwork, stair runner, and office carpet, and addressing urine staining/odor sources in the flooring.
scope: Plaster repair and soot cleanup in the great room, northeast bedroom and west master suite, including patching damaged plaster and cleaning/sealing soot-stained surfaces.
Repair ceilings at light fixtures as needed, then prime and paint walls, ceilings and trim throughout the triplex.
Repair and refinish damaged mahogany woodwork and fireplaces, including window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels, damaged hearth tiles, foyer door veneer, and the northeast bedroom door.
Repair the third-floor tub porcelain chip, refit/repair the vanity panel, and complete bathroom caulking/touch-ups as needed.
Sand and refinish parquet and plank floors in the triplex, stain to match, and apply finish coats per the quote.
Replace damaged parquet and missing inlay border pieces with matched stock, including cutting out damaged pieces and setting replacements.
Treat urine-stained plank floors and seal prior to refinishing to reduce staining and address odor source areas.
Repair and refinish the main stair, including newel post, trim, top molding and rail edge, restoring damaged/chipped areas and finish.
Supply and install a new stair runner after stair work is complete.
Replace the office carpet after finish work is complete.
content.rationale: The move-out walk-through and Feld Architecture’s restoration assessment report document damaged/stained floors with missing inlay, urine odor areas, damaged plaster/ceilings/paint, damaged mahogany woodwork and fireplaces (including hearth tiles and doors), chipped tub/vanity defects, and chipped/damaged stair millwork plus torn stair runner and heavily stained office carpet. This plan funds the quoted trade scopes that directly match those items, without duplicating the already-completed loft ladder railing repair and assessment. Recommended sequencing: Westside first (plaster/paint/woodwork/bath), then Hudson floors, then Carroll stair refinishing (with floor protection), and Broadway runner/office carpet last.

selections.scope: Plaster repair and soot cleanup in the great room, northeast bedroom and west master suite, including patching damaged plaster and cleaning/sealing soot-stained surfaces.
selections.reason: Covers plaster damage and soot staining noted in the move-out walk-through and Feld Architecture restoration assessment report, using Westside Plaster & Paint’s quoted plaster/soot cleanup line.

selections.scope: Repair ceilings at light fixtures as needed, then prime and paint walls, ceilings and trim throughout the triplex.
selections.reason: Covers ceiling damage around fixtures and overall repainting documented at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Westside Plaster & Paint’s quoted paint line.

selections.scope: Repair and refinish damaged mahogany woodwork and fireplaces, including window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels, damaged hearth tiles, foyer door veneer, and the northeast bedroom door.
selections.reason: Covers the documented woodwork/fireplace/hearth tile and door damage, using Westside Plaster & Paint’s quoted woodwork/fireplace restoration line.

selections.scope: Repair the third-floor tub porcelain chip, refit/repair the vanity panel, and complete bathroom caulking/touch-ups as needed.
selections.reason: Covers the documented third-floor tub/vanity defects and bathroom touch-ups, using Westside Plaster & Paint’s quoted bathroom repairs/caulking line.

selections.scope: Sand and refinish parquet and plank floors in the triplex, stain to match, and apply finish coats per the quote.
selections.reason: Covers the widespread scratched/gouged/stained and worn-through floor finish noted at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Hudson Floor Restoration’s quoted sand/refinish line.

selections.scope: Replace damaged parquet and missing inlay border pieces with matched stock, including cutting out damaged pieces and setting replacements.
selections.reason: Covers missing inlay and damaged parquet documented at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Hudson Floor Restoration’s quoted parquet/inlay repair line.

selections.scope: Treat urine-stained plank floors and seal prior to refinishing to reduce staining and address odor source areas.
selections.reason: Targets the urine staining/odor conditions documented at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Hudson Floor Restoration’s quoted stain treatment/sealing line.

selections.scope: Repair and refinish the main stair, including newel post, trim, top molding and rail edge, restoring damaged/chipped areas and finish.
selections.reason: Covers the damaged newel post, stair trim, top molding and rail edge documented at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Carroll Stair & Millwork’s quoted stair repair/refinishing line.

selections.scope: Supply and install a new stair runner after stair work is complete.
selections.reason: Replaces the torn/scraped stair runner noted at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Broadway Carpet & Runner’s quoted stair runner line.

selections.scope: Replace the office carpet after finish work is complete.
selections.reason: Replaces the heavily stained office carpet documented at move-out and in Feld’s report, using Broadway Carpet & Runner’s quoted office carpet line.
